weekly_focus: Foundations first: sleep and phone. Lock those in, then body, then focus.
notes: Never miss twice. One missed day is noise; two is the start of a new habit. (James Clear, yt:mNeXuCYiE0U @ 20:00)
On a bad day, do the Min version. A rep is a vote for who you are becoming. (yt:U_nzqnXWvSo @ 06:38)
Plans beat motivation: every habit has a when and where. Set them in Today. (yt:mNeXuCYiE0U @ 06:44)

habits.title: Morning routine
habits.identity: I own my mornings before my phone does.
habits.why: The first hour sets the day. Light in the eyes soon after waking times your energy and starts the clock for tonight's sleep; picking up the phone first hands the morning to someone else. Finishing this unlocks your blocked apps.
habits.min: No phone for 30 min + 2 min outside
steps: No phone for the first 30 minutes
challenges: Phone stays in another room until you've been outside.
Get 15 minutes of outdoor light before 9 am, even if cloudy.
Tonight, put a book where your phone usually sits in the morning.
Protein-first breakfast: eggs, Greek yogurt or cottage cheese.
Ask yourself "What good shall I do this day?" and write one line.

habits.title: Sleep
habits.identity: I protect my sleep like training.
habits.why: Sleep is the base the other habits stand on. Lost sleep can't be fully paid back, and a short-week, long-weekend pattern hurts health. The same bed and wake times every day, weekends included, are the lever.
habits.full: In bed within 30 min of your target and 7.5+ hours asleep
challenges: Wake within an hour of your weekday time, even today.
One alarm, no snooze. Feet on the floor when it rings.
No caffeine after 2 pm today.
Bedroom cool tonight: drop it a few degrees.

habits.title: Meditation
habits.identity: I can sit with my own mind.
habits.why: A short daily sit trains attention, the same skill that resists the urge to check the phone. Start tiny and grow it once it's automatic.
habits.full: 10 minutes, eyes closed, attention on the breath
challenges: Sit for 12 minutes today, one more than usual.
Meditate before you look at your phone.
When your mind wanders, count it. Just notice the number.
Swap today's sit for a 10-minute NSDR body scan, lying down.

habits.title: Workout
habits.why: ConorHealth owns the program; this habit owns showing up. Logging a session in ConorHealth ticks it automatically. On a rest or bad day, 10 minutes of movement keeps the chain alive.
challenges: Make the start the habit: shoes on and out the door by your set time.
Do 10 minutes of cardio outside before work.
Pack your gym bag tonight and leave it by the door.

habits.title: Reset focus
habits.identity: I do one thing at a time, fully.
habits.why: Focus is a skill that levels with use. One block of single-task work a day, with distractions removed first, beats a day of half-attention. Start at 25 minutes and climb toward 60.
habits.full: One 25-minute focus block, phone outside the room
challenges: Before you start: phone out of the room, tabs closed, water on the desk.
Use Locked In mode for your focus block today.
Take your break as a walk, no screens.
Go 5 minutes longer than your last block.
When your mind drifts during the block, bring it back and count the returns. Beat yesterday's count.

habits.title: Deep breathing
habits.identity: I can calm my body on command.
habits.why: Breathing is the fastest way to calm down without stepping away. The physiological sigh (two inhales through the nose, one long exhale through the mouth, 1-3 times) brings stress down in seconds. A few minutes of slow, paced breathing resets you between focus blocks.
challenges: Do 1 minute of box breathing before you open any app after lunch.
Breathe for 2 minutes before your focus block.
When a craving hits today, do 3 physiological sighs first.

habits.title: No social media
habits.why: Willpower loses to environment. The app locks social apps outside one evening window and keeps them locked until your morning routine is done. Paying grit to unlock early is allowed, but it counts as a slip.
habits.full: No social apps outside the 19:00-19:30 window
challenges: Delete one social app from your home screen tonight.
Go the whole day without paying to unlock.
Replace bedtime scrolling with an audiobook or podcast.
Phone downtime: hand the passcode to someone you trust.

habits.title: No nicotine
habits.identity: I'm free. I don't need it.
habits.why: Unaided cold turkey works only about 5% of the time, and most relapses happen in the first week, so plan for that week instead of relying on willpower. Part of the pull is the hand-to-mouth habit, so replace the ritual. Morning urges are strongest because you wake in withdrawal. Talk to a doctor about replacement therapy or medication; the app does not give doses.
challenges: Have a replacement for your hands and mouth ready before your usual first hit.
Write down your top trigger today and your if-then plan for it.
When the urge hits, do 1 minute of breathing first, then decide.
Book a doctor's appointment to talk about a quit plan.
Launch strong: throw out every pouch, vape and pack today, and tell one person you quit.

habits.title: Night routine
habits.identity: I end my day on purpose.
habits.why: Tomorrow's morning starts tonight. Dim light and no screens let sleep come, a cool body falls asleep faster, and writing tomorrow's first move removes morning decisions. Franklin tracked his virtues the same way, marking the day's faults every evening.
habits.min: Phone out of bed + lights dim
steps: Last-orders alarm: teeth + pajamas 15 min before bed
Lights dim, screens off 1 hour before bed
Write tomorrow's first action + a 2-line reflection
challenges: Set the last-orders alarm 15 minutes before bed and obey it.
Audiobook instead of scrolling in bed tonight.
Write the very first thing you'll do tomorrow before you sleep.
Lights to lamps only after 10 pm.
Ask "What good have I done today?" and replay where the day leaked time.
